correctness.rationale: A zero vertex in any non-full part must see each colour outside its part. Every colour absent from full parts therefore needs two occurrences in distinct partial parts. With t full parts, weight is at least t*m+2*max(0,k-t*m), yielding the two competing bounds at t=q and t=q+1. Explicit constructions attain both and equality forces precisely the classified optimiser types. The finite count is obtained from labelled injections, distinct-part pairs with falling factorial placements, and surjections via inclusion-exclusion. Independent direct enumeration checked 29 complete finite cases, 2,921,552 assignments; proof, not samples, establishes infinity.

originality.rationale: The 2026 singleton rainbow domination paper gives general bounds, hardness, and exact cycle/ladder/prism/Petersen results, but no balanced complete multipartite phase formula, optimizer classification, or labelled optimal-function count. Its bounds do not imply the exact residue-dependent cases. The 2019 Kuzman regular-graph results concern set-valued rainbow domination. A public exact complete-multipartite 2-rainbow record was inspected in full; it permits multi-colour labels and only claims two colours, so the present claim is explicitly restricted to k>=3. Neither direct published-finding corpus semantic queries nor targeted literature searching produced a covering k>=3 result. Unindexed equivalents remain possible.
residual_risks: No negative search can certify universal publication priority; alternate naming or unindexed thesis/paper may contain an equivalent statement.
The 2026 primary source was inspected in identified relevant sections and through document-term searches, not every appendix line; the explicit multipartite family was not found.
The published ordinary 2-rainbow result covers the low-palette case, which is deliberately excluded from the assessed novelty claim.
